items.stem: Why move decisions out of Slack threads into a structured Notion knowledge base?

options.text: Chat is hard to search and decisions get lost; a knowledge base preserves them
options.rationale: Correct: a structured base keeps decisions findable and durable.

options.text: Because Slack deletes all messages daily
options.rationale: Slack retention varies; the point is findability, not deletion.

options.text: Because Notion is encrypted and Slack is not
options.rationale: The issue is structure and searchability, not encryption.
Chat holds text; it is just not a durable knowledge base.

items.explanation: Correct: a structured base keeps decisions findable and durable.

items.stem: Which TWO practices keep a Claude-drafted knowledge entry trustworthy? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Have the knowledge owner confirm the summary
options.rationale: Correct: owner confirmation catches errors the AI cannot.

options.text: Link the entry back to its source thread
options.rationale: Correct: a source link preserves traceability.

options.text: Publish the summary without any review
Delete the original thread after summarising
options.rationale: Deleting the source removes the ability to verify.

items.explanation: Correct: owner confirmation catches errors the AI cannot.

items.stem: Why add a review date and owner to each knowledge entry?

options.text: So stale knowledge is revisited and someone is accountable for it
options.rationale: Correct: freshness dates and owners keep the base reliable over time.

options.text: Because entries expire automatically without them
options.rationale: Entries do not auto-expire; the date prompts review.

options.text: Because it removes the need to write clearly
Because owners prevent anyone else reading
options.rationale: Ownership is about accountability, not access control.

items.explanation: Correct: freshness dates and owners keep the base reliable over time.
